**RE: Urgent Member Appeal for Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Sawyer Iverson
*   **Member ID:** W821798872
*   **Plan:** Managed Health Services (MHS) (Commercial/ACA, Indiana)
*   **Reference Number:** POC-40E31914E1-52376
*   **Requested Service:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery
*   **Procedure Code (CPT):** 29881
*   **Requesting Surgeon:** Dr. Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery 

Dear Appeals Review Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my scheduled arthroscopic meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which was issued on August 2, 2026. The denial letter stated that the "documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." 

This appeal package contains the complete clinical history, physical therapy discharge records, diagnostic imaging reports, and orthopedic clinic notes. Together, this documentation demonstrates that I completely satisfy the clinical criteria set forth in **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1764 for Knee Arthroscopy** (formerly NIA_CG_316), which governs medical necessity determinations for Managed Health Services (MHS) Commercial members in Indiana.

Below, I have mapped my specific clinical records directly to the requirements of the MHS-governing Evolent medical policy to demonstrate full compliance.

---

### I. Compliance with General Requirements
Evolent Clinical Guideline 1764 states that "Elective arthroscopic surgery of the knee may be considered if the following general criteria are met:"

1.  **Clinical Correlation:** 
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "There is clinical correlation of the individual’s subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)"
    *   *My Clinical Record:* I have a 14-month history of progressive medial knee pain unrelieved by rest, which correlates directly with physical exam findings (pain-limited range of motion and positive provocative testing) and my knee MRI.
2.  **Documented Loss of Function:** 
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "Knee pain with documented loss of function: Deviation from normal knee function which may include painful weight bearing and/or inadequate range of motion (> 10 degrees flexion contracture or < 110 degrees flexion or both) to accomplish age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational or athletic requirements)"
    *   *My Clinical Record:* Dr. Reyes's notes document a severe loss of function. I experience frequent mechanical locking and giving way of the knee, am entirely unable to squat or kneel, and my mobility is strictly limited to level walking. My active range of motion is severely limited by sharp pain.
3.  **Comorbidities & Health Status:** 
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI..."
    *   *My Clinical Record:* I have no active local or systemic infections, no untreated substance use disorders, am a non-smoker, and have a healthy/stable BMI of 29. 
4.  **Cortisone Injection Timing:** 
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery"
    *   *My Clinical Record:* My single diagnostic/therapeutic intra-articular corticosteroid injection was administered on April 19, 2026. Because this was completed more than three months ago, it falls well outside the restricted 4-week pre-operative window.

---

### II. Compliance with "Section Three" (Bucket-Handle Tears)
Evolent Clinical Guideline 1764 contains a designated section for severe structural tears of the meniscus:

*   *Policy Criteria:* "**Section Three**: ... MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus..."
*   *My Clinical Record:* On May 30, 2026, I underwent an MRI of the affected knee at `[Imaging Facility Name]`. The radiologist’s report confirms a **"displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking."** My clinical presentation of knee locking matches this structural pathology perfectly. 

---

### III. Compliance with "Section Four" (Symptomatic Meniscus Tears)
Even if evaluated under the standard conservative management pathway of the policy, my records completely satisfy the three-part requirements of **Section Four**:

1.  **Objective Physical Exam Findings & History of Mechanical Symptoms:**
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "When at least two of the following physical examination findings are present or there is at least one of the following physical examination findings and there is a history of mechanical symptoms such as 'catching' or 'locking':"
        *   "Knee joint line pain with forced hyperextension upon physical exam"
        *   "Knee joint line pain with maximum flexion upon physical exam"
        *   "Knee pain, crepitus, or an audible or palpable click with the McMurray’s test or Apley grind test"
        *   "Joint line tenderness to palpation upon physical exam"
    *   *My Clinical Record:* Dr. Reyes's physical examination notes document positive provocative testing on the affected side, including pain-limited range of motion, medial joint line tenderness to palpation, and a documented "history of mechanical symptoms" consisting of frequent knee locking and giving way.
2.  **Exhaustive Non-Operative Management:**
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Ice/heat; Protected weight bearing; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Supervised home exercise; Weight optimization; Corticosteroid injection"
    *   *My Clinical Record:* I have tried and failed three distinct conservative modalities over the last 14 months:
        *   *Supervised Physical Therapy:* I completed a highly structured, 16-week course of physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion at `[Physical Therapy Facility Name]` from February 25, 2026, to June 17, 2026 (spanning 18 total visits), as detailed in the attached physical therapy discharge note.
        *   *Pharmacologic Treatment:* I utilized oral NSAIDs daily for 4 months, which failed to provide adequate pain relief.
        *   *Corticosteroid Injection:* I received an intra-articular cortisone injection on April 19, 2026, which yielded only 3 weeks of temporary, partial relief before my pain and locking returned.
3.  **Confirming MRI Results:**
    *   *Policy Criteria:* "MRI results confirm a meniscus tear; OR Joint line tenderness is localized to the same compartment as the tear seen on MRI"
    *   *My Clinical Record:* The MRI dated May 30, 2026, explicitly confirms a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus. My joint line pain is localized specifically to this same medial compartment.

---

### IV. Absence of Policy Contraindications
*   *Policy Criteria:* The policy notes that arthroscopic meniscectomy is "never medically necessary in the presence of Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 osteoarthritis" and is considered "NOT MEDICALLY NECESSARY in the presence of Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 osteoarthritis... Unless: There has been the acute onset of locking... and there is MRI evidence of a bucket-handle or displaced meniscal fragment."
*   *My Clinical Record:* My knee joint is structurally healthy with preserved articular cartilage. The May 30, 2026 MRI confirms that I have **Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 1** (minimal/early) changes, meaning I have no advanced osteoarthritis that would contraindicate this arthroscopic intervention.

---

### Conclusion & Request for Immediate Action
The documentation provided with this appeal is thorough, complete, and leaves no gaps. I have a severe, MRI-confirmed, displaced bucket-handle meniscus tear that is causing mechanical locking of my knee joint. I have diligently exhausted 16 weeks of physical therapy and multiple other conservative modalities without success, and I have no contraindications. 

Leaving this displaced fragment untreated risks further damage to my articular cartilage. I request that you immediately reverse this denial and approve the prior authorization for CPT 29881.

If you require any additional information, please contact my surgeon's office, Dr. Reyes, at `[Dr. Reyes's Office Phone Number]` or reach out to me directly at `[Patient Phone Number]`.

Thank you for your prompt reassessment of this request.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Iverson
